rationale: The primitive docstring still does not explicitly define whether pi0 is at time zero or at target_t, so the stronger statement that every positive-target single call is wrong is not established. However, the canonical local MODULE.md:42-45 defines all retrodictions as conditionals of one joint process rho on the shared history, and audit_system/CLI accept multiple targets while passing the same unrestricted prior vector to every target. An independent exact-source fixture with T=[[0.8,0.2],[0.1,0.9]], pi0=[1,0], observation S2=B and targets [0,1] returns q0=q1=[1,0]. For any one Markov joint process with this T and observation, the function's own q0 fixes q1 through the Bayesian bridge identity: q1(j)=sum_i q0(i)*T(i,j)*T(j,B)/(T^2)(i,B). Exact rational evaluation requires q1=[8/17,9/17], contradicting the returned [1,0]. This confirms a multi-target temporal-prior coherence defect without assuming pi0's time origin. A stationary-prior control [1/3,2/3] satisfies the identity, showing the scope rather than claiming universal failure. Single-target callers supplying the target marginal can be correct; the public batch must either define a common initial time and propagate its prior, accept target-indexed marginals, or explicitly restrict/check stationary priors. No product or protected runtime was executed, and no remediation was performed.
